title: Unary input initialization
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word, $B$ a natural number, $q$ a rational number, $d$ a natural number, and $[?]$ a register state $[?]$ with fields $p,n,a,b,cur,t,tmp,st,nx,q_0,L,u,w,e,f$. Suppose $|x|-p=d$, every register field is at most $B$, $2|x|+2\le B$, $p=2n$, and $p\le |x|$. Assume that for every $n'\ge n$ for which the bits of $x$ at positions $2i,2i+1$ are both $1$ for all $n\le i<n'$, and the bits at positions $2n',2n'+1$ are $0,1$, respectively, the program started at state $m0$ with the same register state except with $p=2n'+2$ and $n=n'$ has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$. If there is no such $n'$, assume $q=0$. Then the program started at state $u0$ with the given register state has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
hypotheses_covered: Every field of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
For each $n'\ge\sigma.n$ satisfying the unary-block and terminator conditions, the specified state-$m0$ configuration has probabilistic semantics with acceptance probability $q$
caveat: The formal statement's variable named q is the rational probability; the register field q is distinct. The prose denotes that register field by $q_0$.
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural number, $q$ a rational number, and let $d$ be a
natural number and $\sigma$ a register state. Suppose that $|x|-\sigma.p=d$, every
register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $2|x|+2\le B$, $\sigma.p=2\sigma.n$, and
$\sigma.p\le |x|$. Assume that for every $n'\ge\sigma.n$ such that each pair of bits of
$x$ at positions $2i,2i+1$ is $11$ for $\sigma.n\le i<n'$, and the pair at positions
$2n',2n'+1$ is $01$, the program started at its initialization stage with pointer
$2n'+2$ and vertex count $n'$ has semantics with acceptance probability $q$. If there is
no such $n'$, assume $q=0$. Then the program started in its initial stage in state
$\sigma$ has semantics with acceptance probability $q$.
